messages:
alex: heads up — seeing a weird perf spike on a customer workload when head_dim == 22 and KV cache is warm. Flash v3 used to be chosen but lately the picker flips between SDPA v2 and v1 on the causal path and throughput collapses under microbatching. anyone else hit this?

maria: :eyes: this sounds like hysteresis/tie-breaker noise around the head_dim boundary + kv-cache warmup interacting with batching heuristics. can you paste the picker logs?

alex: pasted below. the request stream is steady microbatch size 2, seqlen distribution ~ [8, 16, 32]. KV cache hit ~ 95%. picker log:```[2134567890] kernel_picker: candidate_scores: {flashv3: 0.82, sdpa_v2: 0.83, sdpa_v1: 0.79} selected: sdpa_v2 reason: latency_margin (0.6ms) fallback_count: 0``` then 30s later:```[2134567920] kernel_picker: candidate_scores: {flashv3: 0.81, sdpa_v2: 0.81, sdpa_v1: 0.80} selected: sdpa_v1 reason: cold_start_estimate (kv_cache_warmup) fallback_count: 1```

bench-bot: quick profile attached (summary):
- mode: causal
- head_dim: 22
- seqlen mean: 18
- microbatch: 2
- KV cache: ~95% (steady)
- p50 latency: 12.8ms -> 38.3ms after flip
- tokens/sec: 480 -> 160
flame snippet: `flashv3 (12%) | sdpa_v2 (45%) | sdpa_v1 (70%)`

todd: that latency jump smells like a poor memory layout kernel (sdpa_v1) getting chosen by a fragile probe when kv cache transiently reports high miss-rate during warmup metrics smoothing. we should add hysteresis to the score delta so small score noise doesn't change path. also consider penalizing kernel switches during active KV cache utilization.

julia: also check batching zero-padding. if microbatching + prefix bucketing leads to unexpectedly larger seqlens for flashv3 kernels, the cost model could flip. i saw similar where zero-pad pushed flash path over its efficiency cliff.

maria: agreed. proposal: 3-pronged fix — (1) add hysteresis window (N requests or X seconds) before switching kernel if score delta < 0.03, (2) make KV cache warmup estimator conservative (longer smoothing) and include cache_hit_rate in the score penalty, (3) tweak batcher to prefer prefix bucketing for microbatches <4 to reduce pad inflation.

alex: rough diff for (1):```diff
- if best_score > current_score: pick(best)
+ if best_score > current_score + 0.03 or time_since_last_switch > 10s: pick(best)
```

todd: nice. for (2) my sketch: include `cache_factor = max(0.0, (hit_rate - 0.85))` and multiply flashv3 score by (1 + cache_factor*0.05) — gives tiny boost when cache is actually helping. we should avoid hard thresholds.

bench-bot: ran quick sim with 1h of traces: baseline flips ~ 12x/hour for that workload. with hysteresis 0.03 + cache smoothing 30s flips -> 0-1x/hour. p50 latency regression disappears in simulation. attached simulated picker log excerpt.

maria: can someone run canary with these changes on a single dedicated pool? i'd like to watch KV cache metrics + picker decisions in console (per-route) and check rollout safety.

alex: tagging eng-sre for canary setup @eng-sre-bot — we need 10% traffic to dedicated-canary, preserve same microbatch pattern.

eng-sre-bot: acknowledged. provisioning canary pool and routing rule. will announce when ready. ci-bot: starting Canary deploy for `kernel-picker-hysteresis` -> build 2026.3.1-canary.

maria: one more ask — add two new metrics to console: `kernel_switch_rate` (per-model, per-route) and `kv_cache_assist` (fraction of requests benefiting from cached KV). we need to correlate before/after.

julia: also add a small probe that fakes head_dim=22 borderline cases in the probe harness so we don't regress on this again. put it into nightly e2e perf.

todd: i'll open the PR with the diff + sim results and add the probe; assign to maria for review. alex, can you drop the trace that reproduces the flip into the ticket (GCS path)?

alex: done — uploaded trace `gs://redwood-perf/traces/2134567890-kvflip/`. closing loop: next steps in PR + canary -> if stable roll 50% then 100%. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maria: :rocket:
